Area.evidence_source: Half the prisoners stated that they had not received any type of support or intervention following their suicide attempt, and only a third said that they were satisfied with what had been offered to them. This is potentially problematic as, following their attempted suicide, the majority of prisoners were angry, annoyed or disappointed that the attempt had failed. However, almost half of the cases did not want any other support or interventions whilst those that did most commonly asked for psychological or psychiatric help or relatively straightforward things like a job or a telephone call to family.
